Nightlife Culture · design system

Slide patterns

Every slide pattern the system knows. Each one is shown beside the live slide it came from.

01Cover

The opening slide.

Grounds: blue · ink · pattern name: cover

02Statement

One big idea, with a few sentences that explain it.

Grounds: blue · ink · pattern name: statement

03Statement and two columns

A defining line, then two short columns that unpack it.

Grounds: blue · ink · pattern name: statement-two-columns

04Three columns

Three related points, each with a heading and a short paragraph. Optional lead above and a callout or closing line below.

Grounds: chalk · white · blue · ink · pattern name: three-columns

05Three filled boxes

Three parallel areas, each important enough to hold its own filled block.

Grounds: chalk · white · pattern name: three-boxes

06Text and side block

Main text in columns, plus one thing different in kind set apart in an accent block at the right edge.

Grounds: chalk · white · pattern name: text-and-side-block

07Steps

A method or process of up to eight steps, read left to right. One filled cell may carry the summary.

Grounds: chalk · white · pattern name: steps

08Labelled list

Named groups, each with one or two lines of description: partners, roles, audiences.

Grounds: chalk · white · pattern name: list

09Two by two

Four questions or workstreams of equal weight. Optional label above and a closing line or band below.

Grounds: chalk · white · pattern name: two-by-two

10Phases

Periods of time and what happens in each, with a milestone.

Grounds: chalk · white · pattern name: phases

11Table

Figures that have to be read row by row, such as a budget. For decks that are sent and read, not projected.

Grounds: chalk · white · pattern name: table

12Team and close

Who is doing the work, ending on the offer in a closing band with the wordmark.

Grounds: chalk · white · pattern name: team-and-close

How the patterns grow

  1. Put the live deck in reference/<name>/ (PDF plus one image per slide).
  2. For each slide, find the pattern it fits.
  3. If none fits, compose it from blocks in a deck JSON, add a pattern entry here with its reference slide, and rebuild.
  4. If a block itself is missing, that is a gap: log it in docs/gaps.md — a block changes only when a token changes.
